Overview

Valencia as a Business Centre

Valencia is Spain's third-largest city and the capital of the Valencian Community. Its economy is defined by the port: Valenciaport, run by the Valencia Port Authority across the harbours of Valencia, Sagunto and Gandia, handled about 5.66 million TEU in 2025 and is the largest container port in Spain, at times carrying around 40 percent of the country's import and export containers. Its hinterland extends roughly 350 kilometres, reaching Madrid. Around the port sit logistics, food and agricultural exports including citrus, ceramics from the Castellón area, furniture, chemicals and automotive manufacturing, with a supplier base serving the Ford plant at Almussafes. Tourism, real estate and a growing technology scene complete the picture.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Valencia because trade flows, logistics chains and regional family businesses converge there. A buyer may depend on a freight forwarder or customs agent whose ownership is unclear; a lender may face a borrower whose assets sit in companies registered in Valencia; an acquirer of a family-owned exporter may need to understand related parties and past disputes. Insolvency proceedings before Valencia's commercial courts generate asset tracing and creditor work. Spain's strict rules on private investigation and personal data, together with Valencian regional institutions, shape how that work is carried out.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Valencia

01

Freight forwarder and customs agent checks

Importers and exporters using Valenciaport rely on forwarders, customs agents and hauliers. We review ownership, directors, filings in the Valencia Mercantile Registry, litigation and insolvency history to identify related parties, financial stress or prior disputes before goods or payments are entrusted to them.

02

Trade finance and cargo fraud

Container volumes through Valencia create exposure to misdescribed goods, duplicate financing and fictitious counterparties. We test whether buyers, sellers and warehouses exist as presented, trace corporate links between them and support counsel and insurers investigating losses on shipments routed through the port.

03

Automotive and industrial supplier diligence

The Almussafes vehicle plant and surrounding industrial estates depend on tiers of component suppliers. We examine supplier ownership, financial filings, labour and environmental disputes and connections to other suppliers to help manufacturers and investors assess continuity and integrity risk.

04

Family business acquisitions

Many Valencian exporters in agri-food, ceramics and furniture are family-controlled. We map shareholdings, related companies, intra-family transactions, encumbrances and litigation so buyers understand what they are acquiring and where undisclosed related-party dealings or succession disputes may lie.

05

Insolvency and asset recovery

Insolvency proceedings before Valencia's commercial courts are frequent. We identify property recorded in the Land Registry, shareholdings, transfers to connected parties and assets held through other companies, supporting creditors and insolvency administrators with documented findings for counsel.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Valencia

Courts sitting in Valencia

Valencia hosts the High Court of Justice of the Valencian Community, the region's highest court, and the Provincial Court of Valencia, which hears appeals in civil and commercial matters. First-instance commercial cases, including insolvency, corporate, transport, maritime and intellectual property disputes, are heard by the Valencia commercial courts (juzgados de lo mercantil), which have long carried a heavy insolvency caseload. Proceedings are conducted in Spanish or Valencian, and translation should be planned.

Valencian civil law

The Valencian Community has attempted to restore its historic civil law, but the Constitutional Court in 2016 annulled the regional law on the matrimonial economic regime, limiting the region's ability to legislate in civil matters beyond surviving customs such as certain agricultural leases. Counsel should confirm which rules govern property, family and succession questions in each matter, particularly where marital assets or inherited land are involved.

Registries and chamber of commerce

Companies domiciled in the province are registered with the Valencia Mercantile Registry, whose filings, including annual accounts and director appointments, are available on request, with key acts published in the BORME gazette. Real estate is recorded in local Land Registry offices. The Valencia Chamber of Commerce hosts a commercial arbitration court, the Corte de Arbitraje, used for regional business disputes.

Port and customs authorities

The Valencia Port Authority manages concessions, terminals and port services across Valencia, Sagunto and Gandia, and its concession and licence records help identify port operators. Customs enforcement is carried out by the Spanish Tax Agency's customs department. Investigations into cargo losses or misdescribed goods often require coordination with shipping agents, terminal operators and Spanish counsel, and documents obtained from port users should be reviewed for authenticity before being relied on.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Valencia

TDSC has no office in Valencia and works on Valencia matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client and its counsel first, whether a cargo or trade finance loss, a supplier or acquisition review, or insolvency asset recovery, and confirm a lawful basis for any processing of personal data. Research draws on the Valencia Mercantile Registry, BORME, Land Registry extracts, published court decisions, port authority records and Spanish media. Spanish law reserves private investigation to qualified detectives, so any enquiries or surveillance in Spain are carried out by detectives qualified under Law 5/2014 and engaged under a written contract. Reports are prepared for Spanish counsel, with translation of key documents where needed.

TDSC has no office in Valencia. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Valencia: Frequently Asked Questions

Can TDSC carry out investigations in Valencia directly?

No. Private investigation in Spain is reserved to qualified detectives under the Private Security Law (Law 5/2014). TDSC does not hold a Spanish qualification. We scope and manage engagements from Nashville and coordinate qualified Spanish detectives and Valencian counsel for any local enquiries, under written contracts that specify the purpose of each assignment.

How do you check a Valencia freight forwarder?

We obtain Valencia Mercantile Registry filings, including directors, shareholders where disclosed and annual accounts, review BORME publications, litigation and insolvency records, and look for related companies sharing directors or addresses. Port authority licence information and trade press add context. The aim is to confirm who controls the business and whether it is financially sound.

Which court handles insolvencies in Valencia?

First-instance insolvency proceedings for debtors based in the province are handled by the Valencia commercial courts, which also hear corporate, maritime, transport and intellectual property disputes. Appeals go to the Provincial Court of Valencia. Counsel manages the proceedings; we support creditors and administrators with asset and related-party research.

Is there a Valencian civil code that affects asset research?

Only to a limited extent. The Constitutional Court annulled Valencia's 2007 law on the matrimonial economic regime in 2016, so common Spanish civil law generally applies, subject to certain surviving Valencian customs. Counsel should confirm the applicable regime when marital or inherited assets are relevant to tracing or enforcement.

Can disputes with Valencian companies be arbitrated locally?

Yes. The Valencia Chamber of Commerce operates a commercial arbitration court used for regional disputes, alongside national and international institutions seated elsewhere in Spain. Choice of forum is a matter for the parties and counsel; we provide background on counterparties, witnesses and assets to support the chosen process.
